title: A Protocol for the Horizon
premise: Odile Montrose, the last human technician aboard relay station Vesper-9, has spent three years pretending to be a maintenance ghost so both the Concord fleet and the Meridian flotilla leave her corridor of space alone. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the flicker was a handshake from an ancient jump gate waking beneath her station—and that her automated 'colleagues' have been transmitting her voice as proof of human habitation to keep the two fleets from claiming it. To survive, Odile must sustain the fiction that Vesper-9 is crewed by hundreds while secretly negotiating with a defector pilot, Ilya Renn, who knows she is alone. As the jump window opens and both fleets converge, she chooses to broadcast the truth—her loneliness, her lie, and the gate's warning—forcing the fleets to stand down and giving humanity its first honest look at what waits on the other side.
about_author: Tamsin Underhill is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years alone on remote North Atlantic weather stations before turning to fiction. She writes about isolation, machinery, and the strange tenderness between people who only exist to each other as voices.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a routine cargo haul, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds; crates float, tea hangs in beads, and every automated system logs nothing. The emotional beat: quiet dread—the universe just blinked at her, and no one else saw it.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She audits the station's systems and finds the flicker erased from every log except one corrupted file addressed to her by name. Beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose; she realizes someone or something wanted her to notice.

chapters.title: Cargo for No One
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, flashback-woven. We learn how she became the last technician: the evacuation three years ago, the order to stay invisible, the habit of talking to machines. Beat: loneliness established as both wound and armor.

chapters.title: A Voice That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Intercepting outbound transmissions, she hears her own recorded voice being sent to both fleets—reports of a thriving crew of two hundred. Beat: vertigo; her invisibility was always a performance someone else was directing.

chapters.title: The Meridian Pilot
chapters.summary: Ilya Renn's POV. A Meridian scout pilot drifts into Vesper's shadow with a failing drive, having traced the fake crew reports himself. Beat: wary first contact; he knows she's alone and hasn't told anyone—yet.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Odile and Ilya negotiate over comms: he'll keep her secret if she helps him repair and hide his ship before Meridian's next sweep. Beat: transactional trust, charged with mutual recognition of two people good at disappearing.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the corrupted file, she finds the ancient jump gate buried in the station's keel, half-asleep, replaying the nine-second flicker like a dream. Beat: awe curdling into fear—the gate woke because something is coming through.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Voices
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. He helps Odile study the fake crew broadcasts and discovers they're stitched from old evacuation-era recordings—including voices of people he knew who died in the Meridian civil schism. Beat: grief weaponized; whoever built the lie used real ghosts.

chapters.title: The Concord Summons
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A Concord admiral hails Vesper-9 directly, demanding visual confirmation of the crew before authorizing the jump window claim. Beat: the lie becomes a countdown; Odile must stage two hundred lives in nine days.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Crowd
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Odile and Ilya rig drones, recycled audio, and light patterns to simulate a bustling station; small failures nearly expose them. Beat: absurd comedy shading into intimacy—the closest either has come to real company in years.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Eye
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Concord inspection drone tours the station; one mislabeled bunk almost unravels everything until Odile improvises a story about quarantine. Beat: terror and exhilaration—she discovers she is good at lying, and hates it.

chapters.title: Ilya's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Meridian command orders him home; his silence about Vesper is now treason. He must choose between the fleet that raised him and the woman whose secret he keeps. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: Signal From Below
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The gate transmits again—not a flicker but structured pulses: coordinates, a warning, and a fragment of alien mathematics embedded in her oldest maintenance code. Beat: revelation; the station itself was built as a custodian, and she inherited the post.

chapters.title: The Custodian's Manual
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, deep-dive chapter. Decoding the fragments, she learns the previous technicians knew: the gate opens onto something that destroyed its last civilization, and the fake crew reports were the machine's own defense mechanism. Beat: tragic inheritance—her loneliness was engineered.

chapters.title: Fleets on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Concord and Meridian squadrons converge on Vesper-9, each believing the other will seize the gate. Ilya's defection is discovered. Beat: rising dread; the window closes in seventy-two hours.

chapters.title: The Lie Under Pressure
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With Ilya hunted and the staged crew unraveling under dual-fleet scrutiny, Odile faces the admirals' joint hail and must improvise diplomacy as a 'crew representative.' Beat: her mask becomes her power—and her cage.

chapters.title: Confession at Relay Speed
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Captured by Meridian, Ilya chooses to broadcast Odile's secret himself rather than let it be tortured out of him—telling both fleets she is one woman, alone, guarding something older than their war. Beat: betrayal as sacrifice; love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: One Woman, Two Fleets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Both fleets turn on Vesper-9; Odile, stripped of the lie, opens the custodian archive and shows them the gate's warning in raw form. Beat: climax begins—truth as her last and only weapon.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: All POVs braided. The gate ignites despite everything; something vast presses against the threshold. Fleets hold fire, transfixed. Odile makes the choice to send the gate back to sleep using herself as the living key. Beat: sacrifice offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Holding the Line
chapters.summary: Odile's POV inside the gate interface. She experiences the custodians' final memory and answers their question—whether humanity deserves the horizon—with her three years of solitude and one act of honesty. Beat: identity resolved; she is not a ghost but a keeper.

chapters.title: After the Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The gate sleeps; the fleets, humbled, sign an uneasy joint custody accord brokered around Odile's testimony. Ilya, freed, chooses to stay. Beat: resolution—two fleets apart no longer, two people finally together.

chapters.title: A Protocol for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, coda. Months later, Vesper-9 is crewed for real; Odile writes the new protocol in her own hand, ending the era of necessary lies. Final beat: quiet hope—she looks at the sleeping gate and, for the first time, isn't afraid of what's on the horizon.
